I'm surprised more people haven't cited the Constitution requirement for the State of the Union address. From Article 2, Section 3:

He shall from time to time give to the Congress Information of the State of the Union, and recommend to their Consideration such Measures as he shall judge necessary and expedient; he may, on extraordinary Occasions, convene both Houses, or either of them, and in Case of Disagreement between them, with Respect to the Time of Adjournment, he may adjourn them to such Time as he shall think proper...

A few things here: 1) There's nothing here that says it has to be annual, only "from time to tiime". 2) There's nothing here that says the Speaker invites the President. That's a formality and a courtesy. 3) There is no set format or place limiting how or where the President may deliver his address. It may be done from the Oval Office by either closed circuit TV or by national broadcast if he wishes. 4) On "extraordinary Occasions" the President may convene Congress as he sees fit with "Respect to the Time of Adjournment".

This is a good situation where the separation of powers among the branches of government are apparent. The President reports to Congress, but is not subordinate to it.
